headline: Financial incentives nearly double quit rates among underserved people who smoke, study reports
dek: A national study found that financial incentives nearly doubled quit rates among underserved people who smoke, according to a Medical Xpress report.
body:
Financial incentives nearly double quit rates among underserved people who smoke, according to a national study reported by Medical Xpress.

The item available to LungDaily gives the finding only in summary form. It describes the study as national and the participants as underserved people who smoke. It says quit rates nearly doubled with financial incentives.

The item did not include details of the study design, the size of the incentives, the number of participants, how quitting was measured or how long participants were followed. It also did not name the researchers or the journal in which the work appears. These details should be checked against the full report before the findings are interpreted further.
key_quote: Financial incentives nearly double quit rates among underserved people who smoke in national study
